==English==

===Alternative forms===
* {{alt|en|thred|thrid|threed||all|_|obsolete}}

===Etymology===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*terh₁-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|thred}}, {{m|enm|þred}}, {{m|enm|threed}}, from {{inh|en|ang|þrǣd}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*þrēduz}}, from {{inh|en|ine-pro||*treh₁-tu-s}}, from {{m|ine-pro|*terh₁-|t=rub, twist}}. 
{{col-top|2|cog}}
Cognate with {{cog|yol|dreade|t=thread}}, {{cog|stq|Träid|t=thread, wire}}, {{cog|cim|draat|t=string, thread}}, {{cog|nl|draad|t=thread, wire}}, {{cog|de|Draht|t=thread, wire}}, {{cog|lb|Drot|t=wire}}, {{cog|da|-}}, {{cog|nb|-}}, {{cog|nn|-}} and {{cog|sv|tråd|t=thread, wire}}, {{cog|fo|tráður|t=thread}}, {{cog|is|þráður|t=thread}}. Non-Germanic cognates include {{cog|sq|dredh|t=twist, turn}}. More at {{m|en|throw}}.
{{col-bottom}}

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ˈθɹɛd/|[ˈθɹʷɛd]}}
** {{audio|en|en-us-thread.ogg|a=US}}
* {{rhymes|en|ɛd|s=1}}
* {{hyph|en|thread}}

===Noun===
[[File:Knot on embroidery thread.jpg|thumb|knotted '''thread'''|220px]]
{{en-noun}}

# A [[cord]] formed by spinning or twisting together textile [[fiber]]s or [[filament]]s into one or more continuous [[strand]]s, typically used in [[needlework]].
#: {{syn|en|string}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1961|author={{w|Harry E. Wedeck}}|title=Dictionary of Aphrodisiacs|publisher=The Citadel Press|location=New York|page=234|passage=Woolen '''threads''' were an occult means, according to the Roman poet Horace, of depriving a person of virility.}}
# {{lb|en|weaving}} A [[piece]] of [[yarn]], especially said of [[warp]]s and [[weft]]s in a woven [[fabric]].
# Any of various [[natural]] (as [[spiderweb]], etc.) or [[manufactured]] filaments (as [[glass]], [[plastic]], [[metal]], etc.).
#: {{ux|en|the '''threads''' of a spiderweb}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1922|author=w:Michael Arlen|title=[http://openlibrary.org/works/OL1519647W “Piracy”: A Romantic Chronicle of These Days]|chapter=Ep./1/2
|passage=He walked. To the corner of Hamilton Place and Picadilly, and there stayed for a while, for it is a romantic station by night. The vague and careless rain looked like '''threads''' of gossamer silver passing across the light of the arc-lamps.}}
# A [[slender]] [[stream]] of water.
#: {{ux|en|a '''thread''' of water}}
# The line [[midway]] between the [[bank]]s of a [[stream]].
# {{lb|en|engineering}} A [[screw thread]].
# The continuing [[course]] of [[life]]; the [[thread of life]].
# An ordered [[course]], that which connects the successive points in a [[discourse]].
## A line of [[reasoning]], sequence of [[idea]]s, or [[train of thought]].
##: {{ux|en|I’ve lost the '''thread''' of what you’re saying.}}
## A continuing [[theme]] that modifies the whole discourse.
##: {{syn|en|topic}}
##: {{ux|en|All of these essays have a common '''thread'''.}}
# {{lb|en|computing}} A unit of execution, lighter in weight than a [[process]], usually sharing memory and other resources with other threads executing concurrently.
# {{senseid|en|Q1634115}}{{lb|en|Internet}}  A series of [[post]]s or [[message]]s, consisting of an initial post and responses to it, generally relating to the same [[subject]], on a [[newsgroup]], Internet [[forum]], or [[social media]] [[platform]].
# A [[sequence]] of [[connection]]s.
# A [[precarious]] [[condition]]; something that which offers no real or otherwise perceived [[security]].
#: {{ux|en|a life hanging by a '''thread'''}}
# {{lb|en|figurative|obsolete}} The degree of [[fineness]]; [[quality]]; [[nature]].
#* {{RQ:Jonson Magnetic Lady|passage=A neat courtier, / Of a most elegant '''thread'''.}}

===Verb===
[[File:Needle & Thread..jpg|thumb|to '''thread''' a needle ({{senseno|en|pass a thread}})|200px]]
[[File:Man having his eyebrows threaded for the first time.webm|thumb|A man having his eyebrows '''threaded''' ({{senseno|en|remove facial hair}})|220px]]
{{en-verb|+|+|+,thrid<l:archaic>|+,thridden<l:archaic>}}

# {{senseid|en|pass a thread}} {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[pass]] a thread through the [[eye]] of a [[needle]].
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To fix ([[bead]]s, [[pearl]]s, etc.) upon a thread that is passed through; to [[string]].
# {{lb|en|transitive|figurative}} To make one's way through or between (a [[constriction]] or [[obstacle]]s).
#: {{ux|en|to '''thread''' through narrow passages}}
#: {{ux|en|I think I can '''thread''' my way through here, but it’s going to be tight.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|year=1950|month=April|author=Timothy H. Cobb|title=The Kenya-Uganda Railway|journal=Railway Magazine|page=266|text=The line to Uganda goes up the side of a slope in a series of S-bends, and as the telegraph wires follow the line, from below they look like a forest as they '''thread''' backwards and forwards about six times.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|author=Ben Smith|title=Manchester United 1-1 Southampton|url=http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/football/24503988|journal=BBC Sport|date=19 October 2013
|passage=Picking the ball up in his own half, Januzaj '''threaded''' a 40-yard pass into the path of Rooney to slice Southampton open in the blink of an eye.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150923045517/http://www.bbc.co.uk:80/sport/0/football/24503988|archivedate=23 September 2015}}
## To cautiously [[make one's way|make (one's way)]] through a precarious place or situation.
##: {{ux|en|He '''threaded''' his way through legal entanglements.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|figurative}} To [[pass through]]; to [[pierce]] through; to [[penetrate]].
#* {{quote-book|en|title=Fodinæ Regales{{nb...}}|location=London|publisher=Printed by H. L. and R. B.{{nb...}}|author=John Pettus|text=And when the Miners by theſe Shafts or Adits do ſtrike or '''threed''' a ''Vein'' of any ''Metal'' {{...}} then the ''Metal'' which is digged {{...}} is called ''Oar'' {{...}}|year=1670|page=2|pageurl=https://archive.org/details/31383040991344/page/2/mode/1up}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[interweave]] as if with thread; to [[intersperse]].
#* {{quote-book|en|date=2010-04-01|author=Gayla Marty|title=Memory of Trees: A Daughter’s Story of a Family Farm|publisher=U of Minnesota Press|isbn=9781452915364|page=177
|text=[...] the urban landscape '''threaded''' with parks and trees to the horizon. The enormous sky over that flat line dazzled clear blue or filled with towers of cumulus clouds. }}
#* {{quote-book|en|date=2014-06-30|author=G.B. Lindsey|author2=Diana Copland|author3=Libby Drew|title=Secrets of Neverwood: An Anthology|publisher=Carina Press|isbn=9781426898556
|text=[...] dark hair '''threaded''' with gray pulled back from a face still beautiful in spite of clear evidence of the passage of time.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|date=2021-11-04|author=Steven Mithen|title=Land of the Ilich: Journey's into Islay's Past|publisher=Birlinn Ltd|isbn=9781788853095
|text=[...] landscape '''threaded''' with rivers, roads, tracks, pathways and an airport runway; one peppered with villages, farms, crofts and distilleries. Visitors to Islay, especially those coming from densely populated urban areas, often mistakenly{{nb...}}}}
#* {{quote-book|en|date=2023-05-02|author=Lucy Clarke|title=One of the Girls|publisher=Penguin|isbn=9780593422663|page=6
|text=[...] dark hair '''threaded''' with early silver.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To form a [[screw thread]] on or in (a [[bolt]], [[hole]], etc.).
#: {{coord|en|tap}}
#: {{ux|en|to '''thread''' a bolt}}
# {{senseid|en|remove facial hair}} {{lb|en|ambitransitive}} To [[remove]] (facial hair) by way of a looped thread that is tightly wound in the middle.
#: {{ux|en|to '''thread''' your eyebrows and trim them}}
# {{lb|en|ambitransitive}} To [[feed]] (a [[sewing machine]] or otherwise a [[project#Verb|projecting]] or [[expose|exposing]] mechanism, such as a [[projector]], a [[camera]], etc.) with [[film]]. {{+obj|en|:up<q:usually>}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[pass]] (a [[film]] or [[tape]]) through a [[projector]], [[recorder]], etc. so as to correct its [[path]].
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} Of boiling [[syrup]]: To [[form]] a threadlike stream when poured from a [[spoon]].
